module2_problemStatement.coreProblem: Users need a fast, distraction-free way to count things without opening a spreadsheet or notes app.
whyNow: Mobile-native counting requires heavy apps (Excel, Notes)
Browser tabs get cluttered with temporary counting tasks
No-app-install solution reduces friction for occasional use
painPoints: Overkill apps for simple counting tasks
Lost context when switching between apps
Manual tracking in spreadsheets is error-prone
module2_problemStatement.hypothesis: A single-purpose, zero-friction counter web app will capture users who need quick tallying without the overhead of general-purpose tools.

jobsToBeDone.jtbd: As a user, I want to increment/decrement a count with one tap, so I don't waste time navigating menus.
jobsToBeDone.trigger: Physical inventory count, habit tracking, event attendance, quick surveys

jobsToBeDone.jtbd: As a user, I want to reset the counter to zero, so I can start a fresh count without app switching.
As a user, I want my count to persist across page reloads, so I don't lose data accidentally.

targetAudience: Individuals tracking habits or daily counts
module3_jtbd.userArchetype: Task-oriented user who needs speed over features, values simplicity over customization.

alternatives.name: Native smartphone calculator apps
alternatives.gap: Increment/decrement not optimized; requires keyboard input

alternatives.name: Google Sheets / Excel
alternatives.gap: Heavy overhead; requires account login; slow to open

alternatives.name: Notes app with manual entry
alternatives.gap: No one-tap increment; error-prone manual updates

alternatives.name: Dedicated counting apps (App Store)
alternatives.gap: Requires installation; often has ads or subscriptions

alternatives.name: Physical tally counter (mechanical)
alternatives.gap: No persistence; no undo; can lose count on error

module4_currentAlternativesAndGaps.gapAnalysis: The market lacks a free, install-free, zero-friction counter that works immediately in any browser with instant tap-response and local persistence.
module4_currentAlternativesAndGaps.competitiveEdge: Zero install + one-tap + auto-save = always-ready, never-lost counting.

evidence: Tally counter apps have millions of downloads (e.g., 'Tally Counter' 5M+ downloads on Play Store)
Reddit threads asking for 'simple web-based counter' have engagement
GitHub has numerous counter app repos with minimal features but high star counts
assumptions: Assumption: Users will prefer tap over keyboard input — Confidence: HIGH (proven by mobile UX patterns)
Assumption: LocalStorage persistence is sufficient — Confidence: MEDIUM (no multi-device sync needed for MVP)
Assumption: Single counter is enough for MVP — Confidence: MEDIUM (multi-counter can be v2)
Assumption: No authentication required — Confidence: HIGH (counter data is disposable by nature)
risks: Risk: Browser LocalStorage can be cleared — Mitigation: Add export/import JSON feature
Risk: Users may want multi-counter support — Mitigation: Scope to single counter for MVP, gather feedback

primary: Functional on mobile Safari, Chrome, Firefox
secondary: One-tap increment works without focus/zoom issues on mobile

inScope: No account / no backend / no analytics

definitionOfDone: User can increment count with single tap
User can decrement count with single tap
User can reset count to zero with confirmation
Works on iOS Safari and Android Chrome
No external dependencies at runtime (pure static)

platforms: Modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge - last 2 versions)

phase1_build.deliverable: Single HTML file with embedded CSS/JS, counter UI, LocalStorage
phase1_build.successCriteria: Manual test: increment, decrement, reset, refresh - all work

phase2_refine.deliverable: Polish tap targets, visual feedback on tap, mobile viewport meta
phase2_refine.successCriteria: Test on iOS Safari - no zoom, no scroll, immediate response

phase3_deploy.deliverable: Deployed to Vercel or GitHub Pages
phase3_deploy.successCriteria: Accessible via public URL, fast load

learningValidation.question: Do users actually open a browser for counting tasks?
learningValidation.method: Track if deployed URL gets repeat visits (simple)
learningValidation.kpi: Return visitor rate > 20% within first month

learningValidation.question: Is single counter sufficient or do users want multi-counter?
learningValidation.method: Add optional 'email feedback' link, ask one question
learningValidation.kpi: < 5% feedback asking for multi-counter = single is enough

launchStrategy.mvpLaunch: Deploy as single static URL, share in relevant communities (Reddit, indie hacker)
launchStrategy.iterate: Gather feedback, add multi-counter in v2 if demanded
